title: One Thousand Knocks
concept: On November 13th a nationwide ground stop held every flight leaving Alaska while flights inside Alaska kept flying. Two new things were going in that week. Three days earlier the FAA had expanded SMART, an advisory AI tool built by Air Space Intelligence that predicts congestion and only suggests, to all 22 en route centers. ASI said the stop wasn't a result of SMART, Duffy called SMART completely disconnected and blamed 1980s little copper lines, Mullin said you can't rule out anything at this point, lawmakers had asked in October to pause SMART over transparency and the FAA is seeking a stake in ASI. Then, per CBS citing the FAA and L3Harris, the trace pointed at the other new thing, a router going in at El Dorado, Arkansas during a copper to fiber cutover, devices trying to connect 1,000 times every 4 to 5 seconds. Why it failed isn't final, and per the contractor only 69 of 3,648 new routers were running. Alaska Airlines has used ASI's Flyways since 2021, it suggests and the dispatcher decides. Drawn as Slip, a faced paper route card with no hands, pinned to an evidence board under a question, beside a second tarp that comes off a faceless router in a night vault, and a 4.5 second counting hold.

divergence_note: The last films were a sunless mint afterglow over lilac snow with a faced chalk-line reel and ultramarine chalk (11-18), polar night and midnight-sun honey with a troupe of faced decision trees and radar lime (11-16), a rain-black Juneau night at one gunmetal letterbox (11-15), and a rose-line dusk dome over a survey stake (11-12). This film is warm persimmon daylight and a night vault, its hero a soft folded PAPER card with no hands (honestly the third faced inanimate mascot in a row, varied by being paper that can only suggest, never a fixture or a crowd), its signal colour a fiber cyan reserved for the traced mechanism, and its spine an interior evidence board with real exteriors at the open and the close. Honest overlaps: 11-18 also had a line as a throughline that went slack, answered here by board strings that never change state and an additive payoff, a sealed envelope pinned beside them; the pine shadow sits in the teal family of 11-18 and 11-16, shifted greener; 11-15 also staged an interior, answered by a lamp-lit office board and a vault rather than a doorway in rain; 11-12 also had a fat arrow, kept to one beat.

treatment.title: One Thousand Knocks
treatment.summary: One Thousand Knocks (Explainer winner with grafts, restaged at Gate 0). SLIP, SMART drawn as a chubby folded paper route card with a dashed pencil route across its belly, a worried face and no hands, is unwrapped from under a tarp on a cork evidence board and pinned at its center under red question strings and an IS IT THE AI? header, with a maker's tag, three days after SMART went to all 22 en route centers. The fair case gets full strength: two denial quotes with source tags and no checks, Duffy dropping a copper coil on a CLAIM card beside the board, Mullin in a hearing corridor holding a magnifying glass up to Slip's photo and never lowering it, lawmakers' letters with fog, an FAA hand stopping short of an uncut ASI pie, and a raven tugging a string whose far end ties to the letters. At 71 s the second tarp comes off and the camera dives down a cable run to a faceless new router in a night El Dorado vault mid copper to fiber swap, and a counter climbs to 1,000 over one 4.5 second stopwatch sweep. The payoff is additive: a sealed FINAL FINDINGS envelope with a pencilled NOT YET FINAL tag, Slip's strings unchanged. The open and the button are the split Anchorage apron, a Super Cub flying over the Chugach while a faced jet sits grounded, the cone pulled in the button and a cable crew's junction box at the apron edge.
treatment.judge_reasoning: The Explainer is the only pitch whose structure passes the retention rules as written. The router stays under a tarp until after the strongest case for suspicion has been made, so Act 3 is a real test and not a replay of a known answer. Its 4.5 second counting hold makes the 1,000 tries every 4 to 5 seconds physical for a muted viewer, and no other pitch has a beat that strong. The Suggestion Slip hero is paper and has no hands, which shows 'it advises, people decide' without a word and varies the faced-mascot run as paper that can only suggest. Its faults can be fixed by grafting: a short test, re-pinned denials, copper too close to the suspect row, and a crammed button. The Dramatist's and Enthusiast's faults are structural, because their router lands at 50 to 55s.

angle.thesis: Per the FAA and L3Harris, the stop that grounded every flight leaving Alaska started with a new router going in mid upgrade, not with the advisory AI that went nationwide three days earlier, so Alaska's upside from AI in the airspace rides on getting the cutover right and on blame that waits for the findings.
angle.falsifiability: False if the final determination (c22, not yet made) ties SMART or its data traffic to the router flood, or finds the failure began in legacy equipment unrelated to the new router at El Dorado (c18), which would make Duffy's first copper story right after all.
supporting_facts: The traced mechanism is the upgrade. Per CBS citing the FAA and L3Harris, the outage started at the El Dorado, Arkansas site where a new router was being installed (c18), during a copper to fiber switch (c19), with devices trying to connect 1,000 times every 4 to 5 seconds per the FAA (c20). Mullin said the new equipment was overwhelming the older system (c21).

The first blame missed in both directions. SMART went to all 22 centers on November 10th (c7, c8) and drew suspicion, ASI and Duffy denied it (c13, c14), and Duffy first blamed 1980s little copper lines (c15) before the router finding (c18).

Alaska already runs the advise and a human decides model. Alaska Airlines has used ASI's Flyways since 2021 (c27), it suggests routes to dispatchers (c28), the dispatcher decides (c29, c30), and the airline says it saves about a million gallons a year, a company figure (c31). SMART is built the same way per the FAA (c10).
angle.counterpoint_to_honor: The fair case against gets a full scene. SMART had been nationwide three days (c8), Mullin said you can't rule out anything (c23), the denials come from the vendor and from a Secretary whose first cause was wrong (c13, c14, c15), lawmakers had already asked for a SMART pause over transparency (c26), and the FAA is seeking a stake in ASI (c42). The film grants all of it and then lands on the only traced mechanism, the router (c18), with the cause still not final (c22). Alaska's Flyways numbers are the airline's own (c31, c32).
angle.who_it_serves: Alaskans who fly out of state, Alaska Airlines' dispatch model judged on its record, and Alaska's delegation watching the $12.5 billion overhaul (c44).
angle.second_movement: The old system got blamed and the trigger was the fix for it. And the fix is barely started, per Senate Commerce Democrats citing the contractor (c25), so the cutover risk is mostly ahead.

runner_up_angles.thesis: Trust in AI in air traffic control should rest on investigation findings rather than whoever speaks first (analyst C).
runner_up_angles.why_lost: a scold about press timing with no Alaska stake and no upside, its accountability discipline folded into the winner as 'blame that waits for the findings'

runner_up_angles.thesis: The advisory AI Alaska Airlines has used since 2021 wasn't what broke (analyst B).
runner_up_angles.why_lost: Flyways was never accused, so it cleared the wrong tool; its Alaska stake and Flyways as the human in the loop example were folded in

runner_up_angles.thesis: The real risk in modernizing air traffic control lives in the cutover of old plumbing to new (analyst A).
runner_up_angles.why_lost: it won the mechanism but stated SMART's clearing as settled and said Alaska was cut off when in-state flights flew; folded in with attribution and the not final caveat

open_loop.what: Is it the AI? Planted when the spotlight lands on the left tarp under ONE OF THEM WAS AI and an IS IT THE AI? header card pins over the board, kept as Slip pinned to the board's center under red question strings through the denials, the magnifier, the fog and the raven, paid when a sealed, unopened FINAL FINDINGS envelope drops onto the center pin with a pencilled WHY IT FAILED · NOT YET FINAL tag, a red string now also running to the other tarp's router, and Slip's strings unchanged.

open_loop_2.what: Whose dark desk is that? Planted as a snapshot dropping into the lamp light at the board's center, a shadowed dispatch desk near Seattle where a hand twitches over a screen, kept in view as the fog spares it and in the top-down of the board, paid when the camera pushes into the snapshot and the desk lights up as Alaska Airlines' Flyways desk and the dispatcher's hand taps the second route, THE DISPATCHER DECIDES.
